concerns.text: FR-000 references “See US-1”, but no identifier US-1 is defined anywhere in the document. The same undefined reference pattern appears in FR-001 (US-1), FR-002 (US-2), FR-003 (US-3), and the Success Criteria (SC-001, SC-002, SC-003, SC-004). All cross‑references must resolve to an existing ID.

The document calls the first story “User Story 1” but later cross‑references it as “US-1”. This inconsistent terminology makes traceability ambiguous; choose a single identifier style (e.g., US-1) and apply it uniformly.

Constitution VI (Behavioral Proxy Transparency) mandates that any claim about “neural responses” must explicitly state it is inferred from behavioral proxies. The specification’s title mentions “Neural Responses” but no functional requirement or limitation clause makes this derivation explicit, violating the constitution.

SC-002 states “Total compute time is measured against the 6‑hour GitHub Actions free‑tier limit for the entire workflow” but does not specify how the total time should be captured (e.g., sum of step durations, a single timer spanning all jobs, or CI‑provided runtime metadata). Without a concrete measurement procedure the criterion is vague and could be interpreted inconsistently.

The specification title and opening description claim to study “Neural Responses to Positive Feedback,” yet the entire methodology only measures behavioral proxies (reaction times, mood ratings) and never mentions that any neural inference will be derived from these proxies. This silently redefines the original research question (which concerns neural responses) without the required transparency mandated by Constitution Principle VI.

The specification treats matching Participant IDs across two independent datasets (OpenNeuro ds000208 and ds003392) as sufficient to justify a 2×2 Mixed ANOVA (Within‑Subjects) to test modulation. Because the rejection and reward tasks were administered in separate studies, the matched IDs do not create a true within‑subject design; any observed interaction would be confounded by study‑level differences. This makes the core hypothesis (social rejection modulates neural/behavioral response to positive feedback) untestable with the proposed data, violating methodological validity.

Success Criterion SC-003 states that the output file must contain a column "p_fdr" where every value is ≤ the corresponding raw p‑value. By definition of the Benjamini‑Hochberg FDR procedure, adjusted p‑values are *greater than or equal to* the raw p‑values. The criterion therefore encodes an impossible relationship and validates the metric by a false, circular condition.

The project title and research question refer to "Neural Responses" while the methodology only collects behavioral proxies (reaction times, mood ratings). Constitution VI requires any claim about neural responses to be explicitly qualified as derived from these proxies, yet the specification contains no such qualification. This creates a mismatch between the claimed construct and the measured data, leading to potentially misleading interpretations.

responses.response: Added explicit requirement that neural responses are inferred from behavioral proxies, satisfying Constitution VI.
responses.what_changed: Inserted new FR‑009 stating the inference limitation and added a corresponding limitation note in Assumptions.

responses.what_changed: Rewrote SC‑002 to describe summing step‑wise timestamps from GitHub Actions log (github.run_duration) and storing the value in a runtime_report.json file.

responses.response: Qualified the research question to make clear that “Neural Responses” are derived from behavioral proxies.
responses.what_changed: Added a clarifying sentence to the opening description and linked it to FR‑009; updated title line with a parenthetical note.

responses.response: Removed the unsupported within‑subjects Mixed ANOVA claim; analysis is now strictly Between‑Subjects with a clear limitation statement.
responses.what_changed: Edited FR‑007 and FR‑008 to drop Mixed ANOVA logic, changed acceptance scenario 1 in User Story 3 to describe Two‑Sample t‑test/One‑Way ANOVA only, and added a limitation note about lack of true within‑subject design.

responses.response: Corrected SC‑003 to reflect the correct relationship between raw and FDR‑adjusted p‑values.
responses.what_changed: Reworded SC‑003 to require a column “p_fdr” where each value is ≥ the corresponding raw p‑value, and added a note about the Benjamini‑Hochberg monotonicity property.

responses.response: Added explicit qualification that neural response claims are based on behavioral proxies, mirroring Constitution VI.
responses.what_changed: Inserted the same clarification as in FR‑009 into the opening description and added a limitation clause in Assumptions.

new_concerns.text: Headings still use the phrase “User Story 1”, “User Story 2”, etc., while the identifier style throughout the document is US‑X. This re‑introduces inconsistent terminology and may confuse traceability. Rename headings to use the US‑X identifier exclusively (e.g., “US‑1 – Data Ingestion and Variable Validation”).

FR-005 mandates ≤ 7 GB RAM usage, but no Success Criterion quantifies how RAM usage will be measured or verified. Add a measurable SC (e.g., record peak memory via psutil or `/usr/bin/time -v` and require peak ≤ 7 GB) to make the requirement testable.
